title: DNA Extraction from Sterivex Filters
author: Andreas Novotny
materials: Remove the parafilm and remove Longmire’s buffer/SLB using a syringe. You can use a plastic “tripour” to dispose the buffer and then pour all of the volume in the sink. Rinse the tripour with water after use, dry and wipe it down using a paper towel and PREempt solution.
Inject 720 μL ATL buffer into the Sterivex.

We are aiming to do about 24 samples per day, but you can aim for less than that until you get comfortable with the protocol. Materials needed: Proteinase K, 2mL Qiagen Catalog #19131 0.5 mm glass beads, silica. Molecular grade Molecular grade ethanol (100%) QIAgen DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit, 50 rxn Qiagen Catalog #69504 The kit Includes: ATL (lysis buffer) AL (lysis buffer) RNAse AW1 (Wash buffer) AW2 (Wash buffer) AE (Elution buffer) Spin Columns OneStep PCR Inhibitor Removal Kit Zymo Research Catalog #D6030 The kit Includes: ZYMO spin columns Prep solution

steps.title: Gather reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect ATL buffer, AL buffer, proteinase K, RNase A, and anhydrous ethanol. Place ATL and AL buffers in the incubator to eliminate precipitate. Locate proteinase‑K aliquots (one aliquot sufficient for 12 samples) in the cardboard box in the mini‑freezer and locate ethanol in the CR1 mini‑fridge (and CR2 mini‑freezer).

steps.title: Calculate volumes and prepare aliquots
steps.instruction: Determine the required volume of each reagent for each step, prepare a one‑time‑use tube for each aliquot, add a slight excess, and discard leftovers. Perform aliquoting inside the HEPA‑filtered workstation.

steps.title: Cut parafilm to size
steps.instruction: Cut parafilm into pieces 1 cm × 5 cm; prepare two or three pieces per Sterivex (extra pieces may be needed for replacement).

steps.title: Clean work area and set incubator
steps.instruction: Wipe benches, centrifuge, and all working surfaces with PREempt solution/wipes. Turn on the incubator and set it to 56 °C.

steps.title: Dry Sterivex inlet if needed
steps.instruction: If the inlet is wet, dry it with a Kimwipe (one wipe per Sterivex) and place the Sterivex on a clean Kimwipe while preparing the next unit.

steps.title: Add silica beads to Sterivex
steps.instruction: Add 0.1 mm silica beads (≈0.3 g or three white spoons) into each Sterivex using a weighting‑paper funnel; use one funnel per Sterivex.

steps.title: Seal Sterivex outlet with parafilm
steps.instruction: Seal the outlet port of each Sterivex filter unit with a piece of the prepared parafilm.

steps.title: Prepare extraction blank
steps.instruction: Set up one additional Sterivex containing ATL buffer to serve as an extraction blank for contamination monitoring.

steps.title: Bead‑beat Sterivex for lysis
steps.instruction: Place each Sterivex in the vortex adapter and bead‑beat for 10 min to promote cell lysis.

steps.title: Incubate Sterivex at 56 °C
steps.instruction: Put each Sterivex into a 50 mL tube and incubate at 56 °C for 30 min while tilting or rotating the tube.

steps.title: Repeat bead‑beat and incubation
steps.instruction: Repeat the bead‑beating (10 min) and the 56 °C incubation (30 min) a second time.

steps.title: Add proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL proteinase‑K to each Sterivex.

steps.title: Reseal outlet if lysate leaks
steps.instruction: If lysate is observed leaking, reseal the outlet port with a fresh piece of parafilm.

steps.title: Mix and incubate 2 h
steps.instruction: Vortex the tubes for ~10 s (or gently mix), return Sterivexes to the 50 mL tubes, and incubate at 56 °C for 2 h while rotating.

steps.title: Prepare loBind tube for DNA recovery
steps.instruction: While the Sterivexes warm, label and set aside a 2.0 mL loBind DNA tube for DNA collection.

steps.title: Attach inlet to collection tube
steps.instruction: After warming, carefully remove the parafilm and luer fitting from the inlet port, avoiding liquid loss. Insert the inlet port into the prepared 2.0 mL tube, push it down to the bottom of the 50 mL conical tube, and firmly close the conical tube cap.

steps.title: Centrifuge to collect lysate
steps.instruction: Place the conical tubes in Megafuge adapters and centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 1 min. The lysate will collect in the 2.0 mL tube.

steps.title: Retrieve lysate tube and clean tools
steps.instruction: Remove the 50 mL conical tube, use tweezers to take out the Sterivex and the uncapped 2.0 mL tube, wipe tweezers with PREempt wipes between samples, and discard the used conical tubes (keep one as a provisional waste container) and the Sterivex filter unit. Firmly cap the 2.0 mL tube.

steps.title: Add RNase A
steps.instruction: Add 4 µL RNase A (100 mg/mL) to the lysate, mix by pipetting up and down or vortexing, and incubate at room temperature for 2 min.

steps.title: Add buffer AL and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL buffer AL, mix thoroughly (pipette or vortex); a precipitate may form. Incubate at 56 °C for 10 min (no rotisserie needed).

steps.title: Add ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL ethanol (96‑100 %), mix thoroughly. Total volume is now approximately 1.2 mL.

steps.title: Load lysate onto DNeasy column – part 1
steps.instruction: Pipette 600 µL of the mixture into a DNeasy mini spin column placed in a 2 mL collection tube. Centrifuge at 8,000 rpm (~6,000 × g) for 1 min and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Load lysate onto DNeasy column – part 2
steps.instruction: Pipette the remaining lysate (≈600 µL) onto the same spin column and repeat the centrifugation step (8,000 rpm, 1 min). Discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash column with buffer AW1
steps.instruction: Place the spin column in a new 2 mL collection tube. If buffer remains after spinning, centrifuge again at higher speed (~10,000 × g) and repeat if necessary. Add 500 µL buffer AW1, centrifuge 1 min at 8,000 rpm (~6,000 × g), and discard the flow‑through and collection tube.

steps.title: Wash column with buffer AW2
steps.instruction: Place the spin column in a fresh 2 mL collection tube, add 500 µL buffer AW2, centrifuge for 30 s at 14,000 rpm (~20,000 × g), then discard the flow‑through and collection tube.

steps.title: Transfer column to microcentrifuge tube
steps.instruction: Move the spin column to a new 1.5 mL or 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Prepare Zymo‑Spin III‑HRC column
steps.instruction: Insert the Zymo‑Spin ‱ III‑HRC column into a collection tube, open the cap, add 600 µL Prep‑Solution, and centrifuge at 8,000 × g for 3 min. The matrix may appear dehydrated or powdery – this is normal.

steps.title: UV‑decontaminate consumables
steps.instruction: UV‑irradiate for 30 min all tubes that will be used to aliquot buffers and silica beads, as well as the 5 mL tube of silica beads needed for up to 12 samples. Ensure availability of 2 mL tubes, 50 mL Falcon tubes, racks, pipettes, and tips.

steps.title: Elute DNA from DNeasy column
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL buffer AE to the centre of the spin‑column membrane, incubate 1 min at room temperature, then centrifuge 1 min at 8,000 rpm (~6,000 × g).

steps.title: Transfer eluate to Zymo‑Spin column
steps.instruction: Transfer the eluate to a clean, labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add it to the prepared Zymo‑Spin ‱ III‑HRC column, and centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 3 min.

steps.title: Store purified DNA
steps.instruction: Seal the final DNA tube and store the purified DNA at –80 °C.
